packages.title: Contracts and build bootstrap
deliverables: Reviewed initial commit preserving existing staged/untracked work, followed by a frozen contract baseline commit.
Pinned Zig toolchain and explicit Linux/macOS/Windows native build and test matrix.
Minimal shared contracts for events, providers, tools, I/O, sessions, resolved configuration, JSON-RPC, and ACP host requests.
Scripted fake adapters, ownership/lifetime rules, test-module registry, and planned build target interfaces.
acceptance: Clean-clone bootstrap builds and contract tests pass on each declared native OS.
Cancellation, bounded output, failure, event ordering, and borrowed/owned memory rules are exercised through shared interfaces.
Unimplemented suites return unavailable; no zero-test success or fake production capability.
No runtime orchestration, speculative framework, or unrelated existing file modification is introduced.
handoff: Exact initial and contract commit IDs; compiler/target matrix.
Contract examples, fake adapter entrypoints, module test commands, dependency inventory.
Reviewed path ownership and protocol-profile contract decisions.

packages.title: HTTP and TLS transport
deliverables: Outbound TLS-validating HTTP with streamed request/response bodies and connection reuse.
Explicit cancellation, deadlines, byte/header limits, backpressure, proxy/CA behavior, and shutdown.
Transport interface independent of provider and MCP method/retry policy.
acceptance: Loopback fixtures cover byte fragmentation, slow consumers, timeouts, disconnects, certificate errors, and bounded memory.
Linux/macOS/Windows native transport tests pass.
No automatic effect-ambiguous request replay or credential forwarding outside declared redirect rules.
handoff: Owned-buffer lifecycle and cancellation/shutdown semantics.
Dependency footprint, proxy/CA support matrix, exact commands and native results.
Fixture corpus for provider and MCP consumers.

packages.title: SSE, NDJSON, and JSON-RPC framing
deliverables: Incremental bounded SSE and NDJSON framing usable by providers, MCP, and ACP.
JSON-RPC envelope decoding, request correlation, and protocol-neutral errors.
Adversarial framing corpus and fuzz entrypoints without protocol method policy.
acceptance: All-byte-boundary fixtures cover UTF-8, line endings, multiple frames, truncated input, nesting/size limits, and malformed JSON.
Duplicate/unknown IDs and cancellation/shutdown are reported without corrupting correlation.
Provider codecs need no MCP import; MCP/ACP method tables remain in their owning modules.
handoff: Exact frame/envelope ownership and error contracts.
Corpus, fuzz seeds, commands and observed bounds.
Examples for SSE provider, MCP, and ACP consumers.

packages.title: Single-conversation core
deliverables: One state owner for model request, streamed response, validated tool execution, results, and natural stop.
Injected provider/tool/store/output interfaces, explicit cancellation, input ordering, usage and resource limits.
Typed final outcomes preserving provider replay data and uncertain-effect state.
acceptance: Scripted no-tool, tool-loop, malformed/truncated-call, denial/failure, cancellation, and transport-error cases pass.
Every run has one terminal outcome; transcript/tool IDs and event order remain consistent.
Truncated arguments never execute; interrupted effects never replay automatically.
No goals, planners, subagents, model routing, hidden continuation, or completion classifier.
handoff: State-transition examples, contract assumptions, and exact tests.
Cancellation/commit/limit behavior and artifacts for frontend consumers.
Remaining provider-native integration checks clearly separated from fake results.

packages.title: Provider adapters
deliverables: All three required provider adapters: OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages, with xAI-compatible endpoint configuration.
Configured models/base URLs/credentials separated from protocol grammar.
Reasoning/replay preservation, typed capability validation, usage/stop events, and bounded explicit retry policy.
acceptance: All three protocol codecs pass complete fixtures; two wire shapes are only an intermediate interface check, not F04 completion.
Text, tools, reasoning/signatures, usage, stream errors, limits, and retry eligibility match expected records.
Unsupported credential or provider features fail visibly rather than silently degrading.
handoff: Implemented protocol/capability matrix and credential modes.
Wire fixtures, commands, observed results, and pending live cases.
No claim that arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints have been qualified.

packages.title: Built-in tools and process ownership
deliverables: Optional read, write, exact-edit, and process tools with explicit schemas.
Validated disjoint edits and truthful write/uncertain-effect outcomes.
Bounded stdout/stderr and native child/descendant cancellation, reaping, exit/signal reporting.
acceptance: Invalid/stale/ambiguous/overlapping edit fixtures cause no unintended writes; unchanged bytes and line endings are preserved.
Large output, timeout, cancellation, grandchildren, and parent-exit cleanup are tested natively on all three OSes.
Shell/argv behavior and filesystem atomicity claims are documented and exercised.
handoff: Tool schemas, failure/outcome examples, filesystem guarantees and limits.
Process cleanup matrix, artifact/output limits, native commands and results.
No unrestricted-shell path allowlist is represented as an OS sandbox.

packages.title: MCP client over stdio and Streamable HTTP
deliverables: Explicit MCP 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-11-25 client profiles as specified in docs/protocols.md.

Required stdio and Streamable HTTP transports, discovery/initialization, tools/list and tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, prompts/list and prompts/get through ContextSource in the tool contract.
Profile-specific auth/session/subscription/cancellation behavior integrated into the common tool registry.
acceptance: Independent fake-server matrix covers both profiles and transports, interleaving, bad peers, auth failures, pagination, disconnects and cancellation.
Reconnect rules cannot duplicate effects; server/tool output obeys configured limits; resources/templates/prompts preserve provenance and require explicit retrieval.
Advertised tool schemas stay pinned per run; detected removal/schema changes block affected calls with catalog_changed; new generations become visible next run.
Advertised capabilities correspond to implemented behavior on Linux/macOS/Windows.
After F05, real stdio child cancellation, shutdown, and reaping pass on every declared native OS; process fakes alone cannot complete F06.
handoff: Exact revision/transport/capability matrix and unsupported optional features.
Protocol transcripts, fixtures, commands, and transport/process assumptions.
Real-server interoperability cases reserved for final F13 qualification.

packages.title: Append-only session journal
deliverables: Optional in-memory sessions and versioned append-only linear local journal.
Single writer, bounded records/artifact references, explicit commit/durability behavior.
Crash recovery distinguishing incomplete tail, corruption, and unknown tool effects.
acceptance: Short write, disk full, failed commit, concurrent open, torn tail, middle corruption, and resume-phase fixtures pass.
Committed events require successful configured persistence; provisional deltas are explicitly different.
Unknown effects are reported and never automatically replayed; no database/tree/goal ledger introduced.
handoff: Format examples, writer/durability rules, and recovery traces.
Exact failure-injection commands and results.
Storage-disabled behavior and artifact retention limits.

packages.title: ACP v1 agent over stdio
deliverables: Stable ACP v1 initialization, sessions, prompt/update/stop lifecycle, cancellation, and errors.
Negotiated client permission, filesystem, and terminal operations through the host contract.
Mock-runtime/client harness enabling protocol work before real adapters are assembled.
acceptance: Mock client covers concurrent requests, cancellation races, refused/unavailable host features, delegated operations, and shutdown.
Stdout contains only protocol frames; capability advertisement is truthful.
Native stdio behavior is tested on Linux/macOS/Windows; no draft-v2 dependence or ACP-specific agent engine.
handoff: Method/capability/stop-reason matrix and framed transcripts.
Native pipe results, host operation lifecycles, and known optional exclusions.
Target-client live interoperability checklist for F13.

packages.title: Configuration and explicit customization
deliverables: One strict configuration format, deterministic precedence, effective-config output, and provenance.
Explicit provider/prompt/tool/MCP/session/process/resource/TUI settings and credential references.
Empty prompt and disabled-tool behavior without implicit executable configuration or context discovery.
acceptance: Precedence, unknown/malformed keys, path resolution, redaction, explicit project config, and overrides pass table-driven fixtures.
Resolved settings are frontend-independent; no unexpected credential commands or external loads.
Complete schema and examples correspond to supported first-release behavior.
handoff: Schema, redacted effective-config fixture, and provenance/override examples.
Exact parser/validation commands and outcomes.
CLI argument parsing remains with F10.

packages.title: CLI and JSONL process interface
deliverables: Argument parser and callable CLI entrypoints wired by the integrator.
One-shot/stdin prompt, plain output, explicit resume, config validation/effective output, and a separate duplex foo rpc JSONL mode.
foo rpc accepts correlated prompt/cancel commands, typed busy responses, versioned events, and a single terminal result with explicit EOF/broken-pipe behavior.
Documented exit codes, signal handling, stdout payload/stderr diagnostics split.
acceptance: Piped input, broken/slow output, non-TTY behavior, invalid config, missing credentials, cancellation, and resource limits pass fixtures.
Real duplex pipes verify prompt/cancel correlation, busy rejection, EOF cleanup, and cancellation while output is backpressured.
Fake adapters enable early end-to-end CLI tests with no paid/network services.
Command startup creates no hidden server, updater, planner, or background task.
handoff: Help text and concrete CLI examples.
Exit/output fixtures and exact test results.
Black-box candidate scenarios and remaining production adapter checks.

packages.title: Simple TUI and native terminal support
deliverables: Transcript viewport, input editor, status, tool/error display, cancel, configurable keys, and resize.
Native terminal setup/restoration and non-TTY fallback on all three OSes.
Coalesced delta rendering with bounded viewport/history work using the same core.
acceptance: Unicode width, combining text, multiline/bracketed paste, resize, streaming, long transcripts, cancellation and terminal restore pass.
Native Linux/macOS/Windows terminal paths are exercised; no claim from cross-compilation alone.
No dashboard, widget platform, image protocols, theme marketplace, or duplicate execution logic.
handoff: Supported terminal assumptions, frame/input fixtures, exact commands/results.
Render-byte and input-latency measurements with method and host identity.
Manual native scenarios awaiting final F13 qualification.

packages.title: Integration and release candidate
deliverables: One production composition of all required modules with native shutdown and required protocol modes.
Declared cross-platform candidate artifacts, checksums, manifests, dependency/license inventory, and CI lanes.
Exact candidate commit and artifacts for F13; no publication or final qualification claim.
acceptance: All F01-F11 packages are integrated and their package acceptance evidence accepted.
Clean-clone native builds and deterministic integration checks pass on Linux/macOS/Windows.
No production path uses fake adapters; stdout modes and feature disablement behave correctly.
Required MCP and ACP support is present in the candidate before handoff.
handoff: Exact candidate commit, archive/checksum manifest, compiler/target identities.
Integrated deterministic results and native build matrix.
Explicit pending live/performance/manual evidence for F13; release remains owner-gated.

packages.title: Acceptance corpus and final qualification
deliverables: Early offline acceptance corpus and benchmark fixtures against frozen contracts/fakes.
Exact-candidate native acceptance and opt-in live provider/MCP/ACP interoperability.
Measured startup, RSS, streaming/tool/journal/TUI costs and long-session bounds with raw data.
acceptance: F12 exact candidate exists before final qualification; fixture authoring alone does not complete this package.
Artifact/outcome assertions pass for answers, edits, failures, cancellation, resume, MCP profiles/transports, and ACP lifecycle.
Native Linux/macOS/Windows and configured live interoperability evidence is recorded separately from mocks/cross-builds.
Benchmarks record repeated samples, host/compiler/build/fixture identities, limits, and provider-independent costs.
Remaining failures or unavailable evidence are explicit; affected results are renewed after candidate changes.
handoff: Exact-head qualification report, candidate hashes, commands, raw outputs, and pass/fail matrix.
Measured budgets and declared limitations; no unsupported speed or compatibility claims.
Concrete release recommendation for the owner, with publication as a separate authorized action.
